documentation.range: Arapaima leptosoma was described from near the confluence region of the Solimões and Purus rivers (about 200 km west of Manaus and 21 km south-west of the confluence with Purus River, near Anori), State of Amazonas, Brazil, based on a single specimen (Stewart 2013). It can be anticipated that A. leptosoma is more widely distributed, at least in the central Amazon, because there are no obvious physical or ecological barriers to prevent such dispersal. A paucity of preserved museum specimens from this general area, however, precludes knowing the full range of A. leptosoma.
documentation.population: No information is available on the population.
documentation.habitats: There is no information about the habitats and ecology.
documentation.threats: There is no information about threats to this species. As with other Arapaima species, however, over-fishing is a likely threat, especially wherever there is open-access fishing.
documentation.measures: There is no information on conservation actions in place or recommended that are targeted for this species. Stewart (2013) notes that “substantial protected areas have been established along the lower Purus River (i.e., Reserva de Desenvolvimento Sustentável Piagaçu-Purus with about 7,900 km2 and the smaller but contiguous Reserva Biológica de Abufari). It seems likely that A. leptosoma will persist in those areas because the extensive várzea habitat with numerous lagoons is ideal for Arapaima.”
documentation.use_trade: There is no information about use or trade of this species.
documentation.rationale: This species is known only from the type locality. There is no information on the population status or on threats to this species. Therefore, it is assessed as Data Deficient.
documentation.taxonomic_notes: The species is known only from the holotype (INPA 16847), a 77.6 cm SL, formalin-preserved specimen, which most likely is an immature individual.
